glomeris resource — Manage ownership and reclaim enrolled generated artifacts.

usage: glomeris resource <operation> [operation arguments]

Safety depends on the subcommand; each is labelled below. The strongest of
them: Can delete data — every deletion is policy-gated.

Unattended reclamation is limited to Glomeris-created source-free compiler
artifacts. Native Cargo, worktree and Docker scopes may be registered for
protective evidence only, without deletion authority. Acquiring owners and
retirement share kernel barriers. Default inactivity is 24 hours since
meaningful use, not lease renewal. All operations render JSON; unattended
sweep requires explicit per-class policy.

Subcommands
  native <request|inspect|reconcile> --json
      Writes only Glomeris's own state — never your files.
      Track native task entitlements. Requests use bounded stdin;
      inspection exposes no capabilities and never grants cleanup
      authority.
  create --source-root <workspace> --recipe <recipe>
      Writes only Glomeris's own state — never your files.
      Create one private generation with committed reconstruction source.
  create-cargo --source-root <workspace> --recipe <recipe>
      Writes only Glomeris's own state — never your files.
      Create a new private standalone-library generation, never adopt a
      native target.
  produce-cargo <id> <generation>
      Writes only Glomeris's own state — never your files.
      Compile committed src/lib.rs with Glomeris's fixed standalone
      manifest, not original package configuration.
  produce <id> <generation> --input <tracked-rs-file>
      Writes only Glomeris's own state — never your files.
      Create a bounded standalone compiler object from retained committed
      input; reject external/environment dependencies.
  export <id> <generation> --artifact <name> --destination <absolute-path>
      Creates an explicitly named file — never overwrites.
      Copy a sealed artifact through core-only source access. Exported
      copies stay outside cleanup authority.
  hold <id> <generation> --host <host> --session <session> --owner-pid <pid>
      Writes only Glomeris's own state — never your files.
      Persist acquisition and hold a shared kernel barrier through native
      use.
  seal <id> <generation>
      Writes only Glomeris's own state — never your files.
      Verify source-free compiler outputs after all consumers release.
  inspect
      Read-only, and runs installed build tools to locate their caches.
      Read lifecycle and safety blockers; no resource mutation.
  reconcile
      Writes only Glomeris's own state — never your files.
      Recover persisted intent without repeating destructive actions.
  sweep --unattended
      Can delete data — every deletion is policy-gated.
      Execute only enrolled, independently verified, policy-authorized
      generations.
  authority <apply|grant-managed> --expected-current <snapshot>
      Writes only Glomeris's own state — never your files.
      CAS-update the existing Autopilot authority without overwriting
      intervening changes.
  policy <show|apply file>
      Writes only Glomeris's own state — never your files.
      Inspect or CAS-update per-class retention; authorization still
      requires the existing Autopilot envelope.

Examples
  glomeris resource inspect
      Report ownership, meaningful inactivity and preservation blockers.
  glomeris resource sweep --unattended
      Reclaim verified generations within retention and Autopilot grants.

See also: daemon, actions
